title: Polynomial-Time Block Majority Test
statement: Let $V$ be a language of finite bit strings whose Boolean membership indicator, output as a one-bit word, is polynomial-time computable. For any $a,k,a',k'\in\mathbb{N}$, the following function is polynomial-time computable: on input $z$, let $x$ be the first component obtained by parsing $z$ as a pair (using the empty word if parsing fails), and test the first $N=a'(|x|+1)^{k'}$ blocks of length $a(|x|+1)^k$ in the parsed second component, treating an unavailable block as the empty word. The output is true exactly when strictly more than half of these $N$ blocks, paired with $x$, belong to $V$.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of finite bit strings
The one-bit membership indicator of $V$ is polynomial-time computable
